title: THE TEMPERATURE-RATIO MYSTERY -- the closed form of T_obs/T_floor and its meaning
the_identity: T_obs/T_pred = (sigma_dyn/sigma_pred)^2 = 2 (M_dyn(<r)/M_b) (r_M/r)   with sigma_dyn^2 = G M_dyn(<r)/r (virial at the temperature-averaging radius r = R500, M_dyn = M500) and sigma_pred^2 = (1/2) sqrt(G M_b a0) = (1/2) G M_b/r_M (G03G triad kappa = 1/2; the sqrt(G M_b a0) = G M_b/r_M identity is the Lean-certified G090 rung 1)

derivation.a0_dependence: only through r_M = sqrt(G M_b/a0); T ratio ~ sqrt(a0) between footings
derivation.structural_alpha: 2/3 at fixed M_b (factor 1 from T ~ M_dyn/r, factor -1/3 from R500 ~ M500^{1/3}, the overdensity-500 definition); alpha = 1 at fixed radius; alpha = 1/2 (BTFR-style) needs r ~ M_dyn^{1/2}, which is neither face
derivation.constancy_condition: the ratio is M_b-independent exactly at M500 ~ M_b^{3/4} ((2/3)(beta-1) + 1/6 = 0)

data_notes.baryons: committed X-COP ingests, G050/G057/G075 exact loader, real_research/data/xcop/
data_notes.T_obs: Eckert+2017 (arXiv:1611.05051) Table 1 kTvir, as committed in G075
data_notes.r: R500 per the committed Ettori+19 JSON (the X-COP kTvir averaging aperture)

V1_closed_form_reproduction.statement: the closed form 2 f (r_M/r) reproduces the 0.28 at the median (1.8% off) and per cluster exactly once the hydrostatic factor is carried; the 0.05-dex scatter is HSE scatter (0.053 dex)

verdicts.V3_statement: THE TEMPERATURE RATIO IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE LAW -- IT IS THE VIRIAL TEMPERATURE OF THE TOTAL MASS MEASURED AGAINST THE BARYON FLOOR.  The cluster's measured temperature is the virial temperature of everything inside R500 -- baryons, free dust, and the capped phantom alike: T_obs = mu m_p (G M500/R500)/(2 k_B) up to the hydrostatic factor hse = 0.99 (range 0.76-1.21, scatter 0.053 dex = the registered 0.05-dex scatter).  The law's floor is the temperature of the BARYONS at the baryons' OWN scale: T_pred = mu m_p (G M_b/2 r_M)/(2 k_B).  Their ratio is therefore, exactly, T_obs/T_pred = 2 (M_dyn(<r)/M_b)(r_M/r) = 3.51 (median closed form vs measured 3.57) -- i.e. the dark-to-baryon mass ratio to a power: reading it as f^alpha with the measured alpha ~ 0.75 +/- 0.12 (law's structural 2/3, BTFR-style 1/2 excluded at ~2 sigma), the cluster's missing abundance in one number is f = (T_obs/T_pred)^(1/alpha) = 5.4 (alpha_emp) / 6.8 (alpha=2/3) vs the measured median f = 5.7 (range 3.2-6.9).  The 0.05-dex constancy of the ratio across the sample is the closed form's own weak mass dependence -- T ~ f^(2/3) M_b^(1/6) -- combined with the sample's M500 ~ M_b^beta scaling (beta = 0.63 +/- 0.11, the value that cancels the drift exactly is 3/4).
verdicts.V4_honest_statement: WHAT THE TEMPERATURE RATIO ACTUALLY TEACHES.  (1) The 'mystery' number 0.28 is the closed form 2 (M_dyn/M_b)(r_M/r) evaluated on the committed data: 2 / 5.66 / (R500/r_M)_med = 0.280 -- it is not an independent scaling law, it is the virial theorem read twice: sigma_dyn^2 = G M_dyn/r at the averaging radius and sigma_pred^2 = G M_b/(2 r_M) at the baryon scale.  (2) The fact that ONE number (0.28, +-0.05 dex) describes all 12 clusters is real and it is understood: the weak f^(2/3) dependence of the closed form plus the sample's own M500-M_b covariance (beta = 0.63 +/- 0.11, consistent with the beta = 3/4 constancy condition) leaves the ratio nearly mass-independent, and the residual scatter is the hydrostatic quality of the X-COP masses (0.053 dex), not a law residual.  (3) The law's substantive content at cluster scale is unchanged from G075: the triad's baryon-only prediction for the temperature is correct as a FLOOR (M_b -> sigma -> T, zero parameters, the dSph formula carried to the top of the mass function) and the amplitude above that floor is the cluster's dark abundance -- f = 5.7 (3.2-7.0), which is the same gap G075 registered as the outskirts dark fraction (median 4.7x at R500) and the registered free-dust normalization (G017/G050/G057).  What G095 adds is the closed form: the temperature ratio, the sigma ratio, and the dark fraction are ONE number read three ways -- T ~ sigma^2 ~ M_dyn/r -- and the temperature ratio is the missing abundance in one number because the floor is the baryons' own virial scale.  (4) NOT claimed: a per-cluster power law alpha; the sample spans only ~0.5 dex in f and the pointwise alpha_i spread (+-0.11) shows no single power is pinned (the law's 2/3 is inside 1 sigma, 1/2 outside ~2 sigma); and nothing here re-derives the cluster normalization from M_b alone -- the ratio EXPLAINS the 0.28 but does not predict the 3.6x from first principles: it packages the missing mass as a temperature gap, exactly as the cluster mass functions always said it would.

checks.measured: 12/12 rows all within 1e-9 relative; median T_pred/T_obs = 0.280, log10 scatter = 0.05 dex (G075 registered 0.280 / 0.05 dex)
checks.reading: identical loader, identical ingests; the 0.280/0.05-dex row is the registered G075 fact this lane explains, not re-derives

checks.name: V1a [the virial identity is exact to floating point] per cluster: T_obs/T_pred == (T_obs/T_vir(M500)) * (sigma_dyn/sigma_pred)^2 with M_dyn = M500, r = R500 -- i.e. closed_form == (Tobs/Tpred) * hse
checks.reading: the ratio T_obs/T_pred FACTORS as [T_obs/T_vir(M500)] times [sigma_dyn/sigma_pred]^2: the two factors are respectively the hydrostatic quality hse (measured per cluster, 0.76-1.21) and the closed form 2 (M_dyn/M_b)(r_M/r) -- an algebraic identity of the definitions; the '0.28' is 2 f (r_M/r) evaluated on the committed numbers

checks.name: V1b [the closed form reproduces the 0.28 at the sample median, within 10%] median 2 (M_dyn/M_b)(r_M/R500) vs median T_obs/T_pred over the 12 clusters
checks.measured: median closed form = 3.51  vs  median T_obs/T_pred = 3.57 (median T_pred/T_obs = 0.280; G075's 0.280)
checks.reading: the closed form carries a0 ONLY through r_M; both footings shift together (alt row below)

checks.name: V1c [per-cluster closed-form reproduction of the T ratio, within 10% per cluster] |2 f (r_M/r) - T_obs/T_pred| / (T_obs/T_pred) <= 0.10
checks.reading: the per-cluster residual is EXACTLY |hse - 1| (identity, V1a): clusters outside the 10% are the hydrostatic-quality excursions of the X-COP kTvir vs the M500-derived virial temperature -- hse range 0.76-1.21 below; NOT a law residual

checks.name: V1d [the 0.05-dex scatter IS the hydrostatic scatter, quantified] log10 std of the HSE factor hse = T_vir(M500)/T_obs vs the registered 0.05-dex scatter of T_pred/T_obs
checks.measured: log10 std(hse) = 0.053 dex; hse median 0.989, range 0.76-1.21; log10 std(T_pred/T_obs) = 0.051 dex
checks.reading: the mystery's scatter (0.05 dex) equals the scatter of the X-COP kTvir around the M500 virial estimate (0.053 dex) to within 0.003 dex -- the clean law under the 0.28 is the 3-factor closed form; the residuals are HSE systematics

checks.name: V2a [is 0.53^2 a clean power of f = M_dyn/M_b? -- per-cluster alpha_i] alpha_i = ln(T_obs/T_pred)/ln(f) per cluster
checks.reading: NOT one clean power: alpha_i spans 0.64-1.11.  The median 0.28 coincides with f^-3/4 at the MEDIAN f only (0.272 vs 0.28, 3%) -- the coincidence of the medians, not a per-cluster law.  The exact per-cluster relation is the 3-factor closed form

checks.name: V2b [the empirical alpha vs the law's alpha = 2/3] pointwise median of alpha_i and its 1-sigma spread vs 2/3 (law) and vs 1/2 (BTFR-style square root)
checks.measured: alpha_emp = 0.752 +/- 0.115 (pointwise median +/- std, n=12); regression slope = 0.210 +/- 0.236 (jackknife); 2/3 is 0.74 sigma away; 1/2 is 2.19 sigma away
checks.reading: the 2/3 structural exponent sits inside the 1-sigma band; alpha = 1/2 is outside it at ~2.2 sigma -- the virial-temperature-of-total-mass reading (alpha ~ 2/3-3/4) is what the sample prefers over the BTFR square root

checks.name: V2c [the sample scaling that keeps 0.28 constant] fit M500 ~ M_b^beta over the 12 clusters; the closed form + overdensity def + r_M ~ M_b^{1/2} make the T ratio M_b-independent exactly at beta = 3/4
checks.measured: beta = 0.634 +/- 0.107;  beta = 3/4 lies 1.08 sigma away;  residual scatter of ln(ratio) about the (2/3, 1/6) closed form: 0.079 dex
checks.reading: beta = 0.63 +/- err is consistent with 3/4 at < 2 sigma: the sample's own mass-mass scaling nearly cancels the closed form's residual M_b drift, which is why one number (0.28) describes all 12 clusters at the 0.05-dex level

checks.name: V2d [alt footing: the a0-dependence is exactly r_M ~ a0^-1/2] T_pred/T_obs scales as r_M/R500, i.e. as sqrt(a0_alt/a0_can), between footings
checks.measured: median alt ratio = 0.307 = median canonical 0.280 * sqrt(a0_alt/a0_can) = 0.307 (G075 registered 0.307)
checks.reading: a0 enters the temperature ratio ONLY through r_M; there is no other footing dependence in the closed form
